To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the IL23R rs1004819 and IL23R rs11209026 polymorphisms are associated with increased susceptibility to gastric cancer in a Chinese population.

The IL-23R rs11209026 and IL-12RB2 rs6887695 polymorphisms contribute to the susceptibility of multiple cancers and the IL-23R gene is a key factor in the development and progression of multiple cancers.

IL-23 receptor gene variants are significantly associated with the susceptibility of multiple cancers, and that these genetic variants are also significantly associated with clinical features of cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of drugs for the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease.
the role of the interleukin 23 (IL23) receptor in the development of human cancers and the potential of IL23 receptor antagonists in cancer immunotherapy.
the role of the IL23R gene in the development of cancer, especially the relationship between IL23R gene polymorphisms and the risk of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic variants in IL23R are associated with susceptibility to multiple cancers and the association between IL23R variants and cancer risk is mediated through its association with IL-23 levels.
IL23R rs11209026 is associated with susceptibility to various types of cancers.

the association between IL23R polymorphisms and cancer risk is still controversial, and more large-scale studies with more homogeneous populations and more detailed information on cancer type are warranted to clarify the role of IL-23 in cancer development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a new class of compounds, which are highly selective for P2X3 receptors.
IL23R genetic variants are associated with susceptibility of several cancers, especially in Asian populations.
IL-23R gene polymorphisms contribute to susceptibility to various types of cancer, and IL-23R polymorphisms are also associated with the risk of developing some cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IL-23/IL-17 axis is a promising target for the treatment of a variety of human cancers.
we have identified a novel mechanism by which IL-23 signaling contributes to the development of multiple cancers.
IL-23 is a critical driver of cancer progression and a promising therapeutic target for a broad range of cancers.
